title: BE-Prior: Stakeholder assessment for prioritising emergency patients in the emergency department, taking triage systems into account
summary:
The healthcare system, especially emergency care, is under increasing pressure. Not only are more patients showing up, but there's also a shortage of healthcare professionals, making everything more challenging. This affects both emergency rooms and ambulance services. To ensure patients get help quickly and appropriately, there are triage systems in place. These help determine how urgent each patient's situation is. The goal is to identify those who need immediate medical attention and distinguish them from patients whose treatment can wait a bit longer.

Before patients even arrive at the emergency room, they often get an initial assessment—either from the dispatch center of the ambulance service or the on-call doctor. The question is whether this prior information should also be included in the triage process.

Currently, there are only a few studies on how reliable these assessments are across different professional groups. There are even fewer comparisons between different triage systems, especially in German-speaking countries. It's also unclear how patients perceive the urgency of their own situation versus how emergency staff assess it. In a system with limited resources and potential conflicts between patients and healthcare providers, understanding each other's perspectives is very important. This can help prevent conflicts early on and make the process smoother for everyone involved.

The aim of this study is to understand the current situation. By doing so, we hope to find ways to improve workflows, reduce conflicts, and make the process clearer and easier for all parties. Additionally, the data collected will be used to compare different triage systems and choose the most effective one for Rostock.
conditions: different triage systems in the emergency department

interventions.name: Interviewing patients, triage staff, doctors and the ambulance service to assess the patient's urgency by arrival in the emergency department and determine the diagnosis and resources required for the patient within the emergency department

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All patients of the central emergency department
Exclusion criteria:
Patients from the emergency bay
